DIAGNOSIS READY: Staghorn Calculus (Struvite Stone) with associated Pyelonephritis.

Based on your recurrent UTIs, right flank pain, hematuria, and imaging findings suggestive of a large staghorn calculus, the most likely diagnosis is a struvite stone secondary to urease-producing bacteria. This condition requires urgent urologic intervention and a long course of antibiotics to clear the infection and remove the stone.
